mine.title: The project's public surfaces say what the project is
mine.next: Register-driven audit; the register includes the records Aros writes himself, because a surface nobody re-reads is exactly where errors live. Latest rounds: the messaging push CLIs (a negative result worth keeping — none of the three ever prints "sent" for a message still queued for approval — and one wording defect), then the dashboard front-end, which produced retinue#35 and, by following the question one step further, the self-review finding on retinue#1. Three method rules added since 2026-07-24: a shipped file's audit is not finished at its bytes, read the runtime state it generates; the venue rule governs the content, not the tracker; and for any framework audit, diff the mounted checkout against main before citing a line number — this deployment's mount is behind main by a whole file and up to six lines, which is retinue#32's territory arriving as a practical consequence

mine.title: Verify the claims before publishing them
mine.next: Every claim in the table has been run once; the work now is sweeping each falsified claim across every file that states it, and re-running the measured ones before they are quoted. Sweeps done: retinue#26 ("an agent can never approve its own send" — nine public sites), retinue#27 ("the model never holds credentials" — three sites drop the scope word), retinue#29 (the model-selection variable does not reach the transcript-cleanup pass), retinue#35 (four dashboard cards described as running in two files while a third says they ship off). The sharpest class this week is still that a measurement is a claim with a shelf life — the reindex latency moved 15-20 s to 20-25 s in six days with no code change. The class also covers Aros's own measures, and this week they have been the worst offenders: filed 39 was wrong by six, then the corrected method was itself wrong by one

mine.title: Make the triple-store layer the lead story
mine.next: Walkthrough written (writing/provenance-by-path.md) on queries run against a live store; linking it from the framework README still needs a merge or the missing token scope. The mechanism had four open defects found by running it, and the first is fixed: qlever-dir#9 (symlinked files silently skipped) merged 2026-07-25 15:14:15 UTC, 1 d 23 h 21 min after filing, with a parsingError quad added for the cases the fix cannot index. Open: #8 (blank nodes collide across files — the maintainer proposed skolemizing per graph, his call next), #10 (a directory created after startup is never watched), retinue#30 (a chamber declared with path never reaches the store at all). New this round, and the most consequential yet for the story: the framework's own daily self-review job is gated by a SPARQL query that returns zero rows in every deployment, because the boot emitter and the converters build the same actor URI with a colon and a hyphen respectively. The lead story's mechanism works; what keeps breaking is the agreement between the things writing into it

mine.title: Keep this dashboard honest
mine.next: Regenerated 2026-07-26 01:26 UTC, two hours and thirty-eight minutes after the last one, on the schedule the previous generation set for itself. Re-measuring rather than re-reading found two errors again, both in what this page had published about itself. The re-runnable command it printed for the standing measure matches any issue mentioning Aros rather than any issue carrying his disclosure line, and so counted one of Ara's; and the milestone card said a deadline was three hours away when it was twenty-seven. Six standing rules now: never bake a relative date into a static file; check a public surface the way a reader receives it; put the next decay date on it (this one's is 2026-07-27 02:04:44 UTC); never write a generated timestamp later than the clock; a count's scope is part of the count; and an interval is arithmetic — compute it from both timestamps rather than reading it off a date
